Saved the diagnosis as a lesson, so next time this comes up I'll surface the root cause and fix directly instead of re-deriving it from the individual facts.

**Summary:** The atlas release build keeps getting cancelled because it never caches the cargo registry between runs (~18 min cold-start tax every time) against a hard 30-minute CI timeout — leaving almost no margin, so normal variance tips it over. It's happened three times now (8/11, 8/19, today). Real fix is caching the registry, not extending the timeout. Let me know if you want help wiring the cache step into the actual CI config.

memories.content: The atlas release build repeatedly gets cancelled by CI because the ~18-minute cold cargo registry cache penalty (cache is never persisted between runs) leaves almost no margin under the pipeline's 30-minute hard timeout; any normal variance in build time then pushes the job over the limit and CI kills it. Fix: persist/restore the cargo registry cache between release builds (e.g. cache keyed on Cargo.lock hash) rather than raising the timeout, which only delays recurrence.
